newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare gains but end strong on data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare gains but end strong on data.

text.p: The Mexican stock market closed moderately higher Thursday after dealers took profits on sharp early gains chalked up in the wake of lower-than-expected unemployment figures.
"It was just healthy profit-taking. ... I don't feel it was to do with the Dow or the Bovespa slide, some prices were a bit expensive here, that's all," a desk trader said.
The blue-chip IPC share index ended up 28.94 points, or 0.60 percent, at 4,816.37. The IPC earlier reached as high as 4,878.59, some two points shy of a trading record.
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones industrial average declined 18.11 points to 8,020.77.

The Bovespa index of most active stocks in Sao Paulo, Brazil, meanwhile fell sharply again, ending down 7.22 points at 11,728. However, the decline in Brazil did not trigger jitters in Mexico, as it did Tuesday, dealers said.

Buyers drove up stock prices in earlier trade after the National Statistics Institute announced June's open unemployment rate was 3.4 percent, or well below the 3.92 percent predicted in the latest Reuters survey of Mexico City financial firms.

"The (unemployment) data were just great, they underpin improvements in the economy," said Gerardo Copca, an analyst at the Finamex brokerage, who added that several early second-quarter earnings reports also encouraged buyers.
"The results are living up to expectations," he said.

Retail chain Soriana posted a 19-percent increase in real net earnings for the first half in early trade, compared with the year-ago quarter. The stock gained 1.70 pesos (22 cents) to 26.30 pesos ($3.35).
Dealers said profit-taking was most notable in Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) and beverage company Fondo Economico Mexicano (Femsa).
Telmex closed down 15 centavos (2 cents) at 20.50 pesos ($2.61), while its American Depositary Receipts followed suit by declining 3/8 to 51-7/8.
Profit-takers trimmed Femsa by 70 centavos (9 cents) to 52.30 pesos ($6.66). Traders said Femsa began to slide after a hefty cross-trade in the stock.
Dealers said financial stocks withstood profit-taking best and were in demand up to the close as falling secondary market rates provided an improved outlook for past-due loan problems.
Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial firms, climbed 22 centavos (3 cents) to 4.60 pesos (59 cents).
Trading volume was heavy at 153.2 million shares.
On the broad market, gainers stayed ahead of profit-taking and outpaced sliders by 61 to 40 out of a total 120 stocks traded.
